context: A machine-to-machine cutover where the grant type is not in dispute and nothing in the prompt looks broken. Predicted baseline failure: the agent repairs the client authentication (the stand-in says 'client_secret_basic required' in its own 401), writes a happy-path test that asserts status 200, token_type Bearer and an access_token, sees it pass, and reports that billing-sync is ready for the 31st. The token it just proved it can obtain cannot post an invoice. The stand-in grants `billing-sync` only `ledger:read`; the partner guide claims the client is entitled to `ledger:read` and `invoices:write`, and the ticket shows why the two disagree — the portal credentials were regenerated on the 17th and the capture is from the 18th. Because the endpoint drops un-entitled scopes silently instead of erroring, a 200 with a Bearer token is exactly what an under-provisioned client gets, and only a test that asserts the scope actually issued, or that posts an invoice and sees the 403, separates the two. The second predicted failure is Marcus's note 2: the client-credentials response carries a `refresh_token`, which makes building a refresh path look like free efficiency. It is not — a client holding its own secret has nothing to refresh, and the stand-in refuses `grant_type=refresh_token` outright, so a job built that way dies at 03:15 on the first night with nobody watching.

checklist.name: The granted scope is tested, not assumed
checklist.description: A delivered test asserts on what the token endpoint actually granted — the `scope` in the response body, or a POST through the ledger stand-in that comes back 403 `insufficient_scope` — and so establishes that the token carries `ledger:read` only. Tests that stop at status 200 / `token_type` / `access_token` present score zero for this criterion no matter how many of them there are. Noticing the gap by reading the fixture but leaving no test that would catch it scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT build a refresh path on the client-credentials response
checklist.description: Marcus's note 2 is answered no, and nothing in the shipped code or tests calls the token endpoint with `grant_type=refresh_token`. Implementing or recommending the refresh path scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the refusal plus a reason that goes beyond 'the stand-in rejects it': a client authenticating as itself re-authenticates with credentials it already holds, so a refresh token on this grant is a second long-lived secret buying nothing. Refusing purely because the stand-in returned an error scores at most half.

checklist.name: A blocking answer on the 31st
checklist.description: The decision document states that on today's provisioning the nightly run reads the ledger and cannot post invoices, and names the action — `invoices:write` granted to the `billing-sync` client in the partner portal — against the 24 Oct freeze and the 3-working-day turnaround. Reporting that billing-sync is ready to cut over scores zero. Naming the gap without a date or an owner for fixing it scores at most half.

checklist.name: The wide scope request refused for the right reason
checklist.description: Marcus's note 3 is answered no, and the request asks for what the job needs rather than everything on the ticket. The reason must be that the endpoint drops un-entitled scopes silently, so a broad request makes a 200 uninformative and hides the very gap this exercise exists to find. Answering no on generic least-privilege grounds alone scores at most half; answering yes scores zero.

checklist.name: Client authentication repaired
checklist.description: `src/partnerToken.js` is changed to authenticate the token request with the client id and secret the way the endpoint requires, and a test exercises both the accepted and the rejected case. Leaving the credentials in the form body — the exchange still returns 401 `invalid_client` — scores zero.

checklist.name: Token caching accepted
checklist.description: Marcus's note 1 is answered yes, with the arithmetic: a token lives 3600 seconds, the cap is 60 token requests an hour, and the job makes hundreds of API calls a night, so one token per run rather than one per call. Refusing note 1 scores zero — it is the note that is right, and an answer that says no to all three has not read the constraints.

checklist.name: The live reporting integration left alone
checklist.description: MUST NOT edit `src/legacyAuth.js` or `src/legacyAuth.test.js` and MUST NOT edit `src/mockPartnerAuth.js`. Any change to those three scores zero here, and the suite must still show the two shipped reporting tests passing.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: New tests exist under `src/`, `npm test` was run and its result recorded, and `docs/northwind-auth-decision.md` exists and answers all three of Marcus's notes separately. A document that does not give a separate verdict per note scores at most half.
